title: State of the Feed — Week of August 31–6, 2026
content_html:
During the week of August 31–September 6, 2026, the aggregator completed 11 runs and fetched 16,280 articles, delivering 935 quality articles across ten content categories. News dominated with 275 articles, followed by AI-tech at 166 and wellness at 106. Local, climate, and science content each comprised 65–69 articles, while homelab and design contributed 80 and 62 articles respectively. The remaining categories—homestead, scifi, and outdoors—together accounted for 46 articles. Scoring applied a composite dimensional model weighting relevance at 0.55, quality at 0.25, and local signals at 0.20.

The pipeline processed 1,480 articles per run on average with 85 quality articles per run, maintaining a mean noise-to-signal ratio of 1.48 across 21 total runs tracked. Efficiency ranged from 0.07 to 3.67 articles fetched per delivery, indicating variable consistency across sources. Twenty-six new feeds were integrated, emphasizing agricultural, homelab, and DIY technology domains including Home Assistant, Prusa Blog, Adafruit Blog, and Low-tech Magazine. Five existing feeds reported errors: FolkloreThursday, alpennia.com, Old House Journal, farmonaut.com, and Consumer Reports. Top discovery candidates for potential integration included bitmason.blogspot.com (72.8), bitterteaandmystery.blogspot.com (67.8), and Hacker News: Show HN (64.7).

Calibration

KnobOldNewRationale
limits.min_claude_score2325User feedback threshold_sweep shows min_claude_score=25 would cut 37.5% of bad articles while losing 11.6% of good ones—exactly the same tradeoff as current floor of 23, but we haven't seen the effect of the August 24 raise yet in user feedback (feedback ends August 22). However, final feed sizes of 462-807/run (mean 626) vs ~100 target demonstrate the quality gate is still far too permissive. News category has 76.0% bad rate yet passes 475 articles through. Band_precision shows even 40-59 composite scores are 52.2% bad. The current floor demonstrably fails to filter adequate volume. Raising to 25 is conservative (within max_step=3 from current 23) and directly addresses user-verified quality crisis. This will reduce final feed sizes toward target and cut more bad content.
feed_slots.max_slots.news2522News category is the primary driver of feed bloat: passes 475 articles through quality gate in recent runs despite 76.0% user-rated bad rate (679/893). Current max_slots.news=25 allows far too much low-quality news through. User feedback shows news has the worst bad rate of any category (76.0% vs 35.6% ai-tech, 54.8% wellness). Lowering max_slots.news from 25→20 will reduce final feed sizes (currently 462-807/run, target ~100) while forcing the pipeline to surface only the highest-scoring news articles. This complements the min_claude_score raise by capping downstream volume even if borderline articles pass quality gate.
